notes.content: disktest.sh now defaults to guided interactive mode on TTYs, supports --non-interactive for automation, includes interactive mode and disk selection, repeatable/comma-separated --device targeting, and writes per-disk reports under the run log directory's reports/ subdirectory.

fulltest.sh now emits explicit permission warnings before rebuild/reclone actions when build directories or cloned repos are root-owned/unwritable. The build directory startup preflight warns on existing unwritable ./build and clean/rebuild paths now explain ownership fixes.

test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh is an experimental prepare-then-run variant of fulltest.sh. It keeps the stable fulltest.sh unchanged while separating detect, prepare-selected-tests, run-selected-tests, and summary phases.

disktest.sh interactive TTY flow now includes mode selection plus checkbox-style disk selection with arrow keys to move, space to toggle, enter to confirm, a to toggle all, and q to cancel. Default on TTY is guided interactive mode; use --non-interactive for automation.

fulltest.sh remains the stable production GPU validation path. test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh is the experimental refactor lane for prepare-selected-tests-first behavior and should be validated on real GPU hosts before replacing fulltest.sh.

gpu-fulltest-v2.sh has fresh verification evidence for a mocked cuda-samples flow: prepare runs before execution, successful prep is reported in summary, and prep failures stop execution early with a prepare-failed summary.
As of 2026-04-10, repository is clean at main with latest human-readable decisions in docs/project-decisions.md and experimental GPU flow work isolated in test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh.
Fixed disktest fio timeout/subshell bug causing 'FIO_BW_READ: unbound variable' under set -u by keeping run_fio execution in same shell scope and initializing fio metric vars. Commit 05c56ba pushed.

Improved disktest fio diagnostics: auto-select fio ioengine (io_uring/libaio/psync/sync), capture per-job stderr logs, and include error detail in WARN output for exit code 1. Added stderr artifacts to per-disk reports. Commit 563d9fd pushed.
Updated docs/disktest.md to clarify no auto-sudo behavior, raw-device permission safety checks, permission-denied fio symptom/remediation, and fio stderr artifact logs. Commit 31be1b5 pushed.

disktest interactive mode now warns non-root operators that quick/full/stress require sudo and suggests rerun command after mode selection; non-health safety checks enforce raw read/write permission before fio. Commit 99dd75f pushed.
Added non-interactive sudo warning path to disktest for quick/full/stress when not root, with rerun hint; documented behavior in docs/disktest.md. Commit 7986aaa pushed.

Improved PyTorch benchmark diagnostics in fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh: torchrun output is mirrored to a temp transcript, failure summaries extract local_rank/exitcode clues, failed DDP repro scripts are kept in /tmp, and docs note the richer failure output. Commit 1ac4e63 pushed.

Added Python runtime warning to fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh for PyTorch benchmark paths: logs active python3 and warns when Python 3.12+ is detected due to known torch.distributed/torchrun segfault history. Docs updated. Commit 28d6f45 pushed.

base-install.sh and amd-base-install.sh now install stress-ng, fio, lm-sensors, and uv; uv is installed via Astral's standalone installer to /usr/local/bin and removed during uninstall cleanup. Commit 9bfdebf pushed.

test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh now prototypes a new node-stress mode that runs stress-ng CPU + RAM pressure together with the existing GPU stress backend for a user-defined duration in minutes (default 5). The stable fulltest.sh remains unchanged until the experimental lane is validated. Commit 9bfdebf pushed.

test/fulltest.sh now mirrors the validated node-stress mode from gpu-fulltest-v2.sh: concurrent stress-ng CPU + RAM load plus GPU burn, selectable with --node-stress-minutes (default 5), while preserving the existing GPU-only stress test. Commit pending at time of memory update.

Added standalone test/cpu-ram-stress.sh for CPU + RAM isolation using stress-ng only. It defaults to a 5-minute run, supports operator-tunable worker counts and reserve memory, auto-installs stress-ng when available and root is present, and is documented in docs/cpu-ram-stress.md and README.md.

base-install.sh now installs repo-root .aliases into the target user home as ~/.aliases, adds managed source blocks for ~/.bashrc and ~/.zshrc, and generates ~/.aliases.fish for fish with config.fish sourcing the generated file. Uninstall cleanup removes the managed alias blocks and fish wrapper file.
Added docs/cpu-test.md for test/cpu-test.sh, documenting the single-logical-CPU stress flow with socket0/socket1 selection, per-CPU runtime control, temperature logging, and resume/log files.

cpu-test.sh now writes each run into a per-run directory under /tmp by default, with optional --run-dir override for reusing the same transcript/progress state. The script still supports socket-aware single-CPU stress, resume markers, and optional temperature snapshots.
base-install.sh now also provisions the target user SSH authorized key and a passwordless sudoers drop-in when absent, in addition to copying repo aliases and installing uv/stress packages.
base-install.sh now adds the repo SSH authorized key for the target user, creates a passwordless sudoers drop-in when absent, and removes both managed access artifacts again during uninstall.

Added install/user-bootstrap.sh as a standalone helper for creating or updating a local user, installing an SSH authorized key, and granting passwordless sudo without rerunning the full base-install flow.
install/user-bootstrap.sh now accepts SSH key material from a repo-managed named key, a local file, or pasted text via --key-name, --key-file, and --key-text, with no silent default key fallback.

base-install.sh and amd-base-install.sh now both disable PCIe ASPM at boot via a managed GRUB drop-in at /etc/default/grub.d/99-infra-pcie-aspm.cfg that appends pcie_aspm=off and is removed on uninstall.

cpu-test.sh now writes stress_summary.txt in the per-run directory, updates it after each CPU, and flushes the run artifacts so a hang or power loss leaves a usable checkpoint alongside stress_test_log.txt and stress_progress.txt.

cpu-test.sh now operates at the CPU socket/package level instead of one logical thread at a time: each socket target runs stress-ng across all logical CPUs on that socket, defaults its run directory to /var/tmp for reboot-survivable checkpoints, supports --status to inspect saved state, and supports --reset-state to clear residue before retesting.

cpu-test.sh now supports both socket-level and per-thread targeting via --granularity socket|thread. Socket remains the default for package-level fault isolation, while thread restores the one-logical-CPU-at-a-time mode with the same run-dir, --status, and --reset-state crash/retest workflow.

cpu-test.sh now defaults its state directory to /var/tmp/cpu-test, supports --status without requiring --run-dir, supports --reset-status to clear summary/progress and exit without testing, and no longer stops after the first successful target because the pass/fail counters were changed to avoid set -e arithmetic-status exits.

cpu-test.sh now defaults to 300 seconds per target instead of 60 seconds, while retaining socket-level default targeting, optional per-thread granularity, stable /var/tmp/cpu-test status storage, and reset/status workflows.

Added install/install-raid.sh as an opt-in RAID / ESP redundancy installer. By default it stages the RAID helper scripts only; --activate is required to install and enable the apt hook and systemd timer/service, and non-RAID hosts remain unaffected unless the lane is explicitly activated. Documented the lane in docs/project-decisions.md, README.md, and install/raid/INSTALL.md.

cpu-test.sh default runtime is 300 seconds per target, docs/cpu-test.md now matches that default, and the help/status paths were re-verified. No active saved run state currently exists under /var/tmp/cpu-test.

Added Ubuntu 26.04 support to base-install.sh and a preview AMD 26.04 lane to amd-base-install.sh using AMD 31.30 preview repos plus amdrocm7.13. Updated README and docs to mark the AMD 26.04 path experimental.

Updated README and the base-install / amd-base-install quick-start docs with explicit Ubuntu 26.04 notes: NVIDIA base-install auto-maps ubuntu2604, AMD base-install auto-selects the 31.30/amdrocm7.13 preview lane.

Added explicit NVIDIA GPU stack freeze support: base-install.sh now warns when held NVIDIA/CUDA packages are present, supports --freeze-gpu-stack and --unfreeze-gpu-stack, re-holds after validation when requested, and ships a new install/nvidia-stack-hold.sh helper for hold/unhold/status workflows.
Documented the NVIDIA freeze workflow in README.md and docs/base-install.md, including the new helper script, the install copy list, and the rerun/unhold maintenance path.
Extended install/provision.sh to pass --freeze-gpu-stack and --unfreeze-gpu-stack through to base-install.sh stage 1, with mutual-exclusion validation and updated orchestrator usage text.
Updated README quick-start guidance to mention NVIDIA freeze/unfreeze passthrough through the orchestrated provision.sh flow.
Extended amd-base-install.sh and provision-amd.sh to accept the same freeze/unfreeze flags for CLI symmetry, but documented that AMD still uses repo pinning rather than apt-mark holds.
Updated README and docs/project-decisions.md to explain that AMD accepts freeze/unfreeze flags only for symmetry and that repo pinning remains the actual control mechanism.
Added install/amd-stack-pin.sh as the operator-facing helper for inspecting or restoring the AMD ROCm apt pin, and wired it into amd-base-install.sh warnings plus README/docs references.
Updated README.md, docs/amd-base-install.md, and docs/project-decisions.md to surface the AMD ROCm pin helper, including manual and orchestrated quick-start references.
Updated provision-amd.sh --status output to point operators at amd-stack-pin.sh --status for quick AMD ROCm pin inspection.

Adjusted test/fulltest.sh summary handling so sustained compute stress and node-stress thermal/performance-only outcomes become remarks instead of failures, and binary/build unavailability is reported under NOT BEING RUN.
Updated docs/fulltest.md to match the new stress summary behavior: thermal/performance-only cases are remarks, and unavailable backends are called out as NOT BEING RUN.

Mirrored the new summary classification rules into test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh: stress thermal/performance-only cases are remarks, unavailable stress backends and missing stress-ng are listed under NOT BEING RUN, and the summary now prints remarks separately.
Updated docs/gpu-fulltest-v2.md to describe the experimental lane's new remark-based stress reporting and NOT BEING RUN handling for unavailable backends.

Relaxed the stress failure gate in test/fulltest.sh and test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh so burn exits caused only by performance or thermal-soft-throttle conditions (including SW_Thermal) become remarks instead of failures; only hardware-crash indicators still fail the run.

Adjusted CUDA samples handling in test/fulltest.sh and test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh so source/layout/build misses are recorded as NOT BEING RUN rather than failing the test; fulltest now locates deviceQuery across the current cuda-samples directory layouts.
Updated docs/fulltest.md and docs/gpu-fulltest-v2.md to describe the CUDA samples NOT BEING RUN handling for source/layout/build availability issues.

Added post-stress-recovery as a default end-of-run GPU sanity check in fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh. It verifies GPU enumeration, scans recovery-window kernel logs for Xid/reset/bus-drop style errors, and treats leftover thermal residue as remarks with a configurable cooldown window.

Added gpu-policy as an optional selectable GPU policy test in fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh. It is advisory by default, can be made strict with GPU_POLICY_STRICT=1, and supports persistence mode plus idle temperature and power-limit thresholds via GPU_POLICY_* environment variables.

Added 12V-2x6 / 12VHPWR sustained power-anomaly detection to both fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh. The detector records burn telemetry, treats anomalies as remarks by default via POWER_ANOMALY_AS_REMARK=1, and aligns the stable and experimental suites' stress summaries and docs with the out-of-band IPMI power-cycle recovery guidance.

Mirrored the 12V-2x6 / 12VHPWR early-warning methodology into docs/gpu-fulltest-v2.md so the experimental lane matches docs/fulltest.md; README and docs links were also cleaned back to repo-relative paths.

Tightened the 12V-2x6 / 12VHPWR detector in fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh with a relative power threshold floor (max 25W or 6% of peer median), explicit no-fan-telemetry skip handling, flagged-GPU index reporting in remarks, and self-contained burn-monitor state resets.

Added a documented future-improvement plan for the 12V-2x6 / 12VHPWR power-anomaly detector: standalone replay analysis for archived telemetry, late-onset anomaly detection, and a later policy review for the remark-only default.

Added test/code.sh plus the code test lane to fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh. The new path compiles test/code.cu with nvcc when available, loops across every visible GPU using logical device IDs 0..N-1, honors CUDA_CODE_SECONDS (default 15s in-suite), and records NOT BEING RUN when nvcc is unavailable.

Future code.cu improvement ideas are deferred for later revisit: add a mixed compute+memory mode, parameterize launch geometry, add a warmup phase, expose better CLI flags, and consider an optional parallel multi-GPU mode. Current default remains the simple compute stress lane.

base-install.sh and amd-base-install.sh should not install yq via apt. yq is now fetched from the official mikefarah/yq GitHub latest binary for the host architecture, installed to /usr/local/bin/yq, and removed during uninstall cleanup.

base-install.sh now supports --no-gpu-stack to skip the NVIDIA driver, CUDA toolkit, cuDNN, DCGM, and gpu-burn path while still installing the general host tooling and recovery setup. The option also skips NVIDIA repo/Secure Boot checks, omits graphics-drivers PPA and kernel header installation, and leaves the host-tooling-only path documented in docs/base-install.md and README.md.

Added an operator entry matrix to README.md that maps common intents (fresh NVIDIA node, fresh AMD node, host tooling only, validation, live-root rebuild, live ISO build, and emergency reboot / IPMI recovery) to the correct primary script.

Added install/build-gpu-liveiso.sh as a standalone helper that builds a bootable gpu-test live ISO directly from a mounted USB root filesystem. It no longer depends on rebuild-gpu-livefs.sh; it copies and generalizes the source rootfs, rebuilds the live boot stack in chroot, stages a GRUB live layout, and emits /srv/iso/gpu-test.iso. Documented in docs/build-gpu-liveiso.md and linked from README.md and docs/project-decisions.md.

Added install/autologin.sh as a reversible graphical autologin helper for the current sudo user. It supports enabling, disabling, and status checks across GDM3, LightDM, and SDDM, and documents that it is separate from install/super-ezc.sh, which only handles tty1 autologin.

Added install/console-autologin.sh as the reversible tty1 console autologin helper for the current sudo user. install/super-ezc.sh is now only a compatibility wrapper that preserves the old ezc-specific enable behavior.

fulltest.sh and gpu-fulltest-v2.sh now support excluding named tests by prefixing the test with '-' (for example -code) or with --exclude <test>. Multiple exclusions are supported in a single run by repeating the flag or prefix (for example -code -memtest or --exclude code --exclude memtest). Exclusions are applied after normal selection so operators can keep the rest of the suite running without editing the test list.

Stable test/fulltest.sh now centralizes PyTorch runtime handling: it prefers the base-install.sh managed Python 3.11 runtime, falls back to system Python 3.10-3.12 when base-install has not run, rebuilds stale build/pytorch-venv environments when their base interpreter mismatches, and runs DDP, PCIe load, clock load, and PyTorch stress fallback through the same isolated venv. Added test/fulltest-python-runtime-test.sh regression coverage and updated README/docs.

Stable test/fulltest.sh now includes three opt-in deep hardware diagnostics: pcie-errors compares PCIe replay counters around CUDA P2P traffic and scans available fatal/uncorrectable PCIe logs; memory-health classifies ECC, retired-page, row-remapper, and repair-state data; fabric-health checks DCGM NVLink/NVSwitch state and generation-specific error-counter deltas. Unsupported capabilities are NOT BEING RUN, counters are never cleared, and none of these tests are in DEFAULT_TESTS.

Stable test/fulltest.sh installs only torch in its shared Python runtime. torchvision, torchaudio, and accelerate are unused optional packages and must not gate PCIe, clock, stress, or DDP tests. Runtime preparation verifies CUDA visibility and venv-owned torchrun; test/fulltest-python-runtime-test.sh covers unavailable optional packages.

test/vllm-benchmark-test.sh is an opt-in post-provision model/agent evaluation, separate from fulltest.sh and the provision orchestrators. The NVIDIA backend uses pinned vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1-cu129 for the supported NVIDIA 575 driver lane. The AMD backend targets R9700S-class gfx120X GPUs with pinned rocm/vllm:rocm7.13.0_gfx120X-all_ubuntu24.04_py3.13_pytorch_2.10.0_vllm_0.19.1, maps /dev/kfd and /dev/dri, selects GPUs with ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES, runs eager mode, and rejects that default image on other AMD architectures. Harbor 0.20.0 runs through isolated uv-managed Python 3.12, so neither backend alters the base-install managed Python 3.11 runtime. The default Ornith revision is immutable, the API is localhost-only, cleanup targets only the named backend-specific container, and artifacts live under test/logs/vllm-benchmark/.

The vLLM benchmark default terminal-bench@2.0 run measures model/agent task success rather than vLLM throughput. Default max context is 16K, so its score is not directly comparable with published 128K-context results or runs using different model revisions, images, parsers, agents, concurrency, or datasets.

test/vllm-benchmark-test.sh names its preserved 35B/16K default ornith-35b-practical and provides an explicit backend-independent ornith-397b-published profile. The published profile pins Ornith-1.0-397B revision 5e3e761811e804c295c1d3c0ce68b21da6154209, terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@6, 128K context, Qwen3 vLLM parsers, Harbor JSON parsing, temperature/top-p 1.0, and 32 CPU / 49152 MB task overrides. GPU selection and tensor parallelism remain operator-controlled; explicit profile-setting overrides are order-independent and recorded as profile_modified.

The ornith-397b-published profile reproduces only publicly available benchmark settings, not the reported score exactly. The original Harbor patch, immutable dataset snapshot, and absolute four-hour timeout override are undisclosed. The wrapper pins Harbor 0.20.0 and dataset snapshot @6, keeps dataset task-specific timeouts, defaults to one attempt per task, and allows operators to forward --n-attempts 5.

test/vllm-benchmark-test.sh defaults to --backend auto. Auto selects NVIDIA only when nvidia-smi reports GPU indices, selects AMD only when rocminfo reports gfx agents and /dev/kfd plus /dev/dri exist, rejects mixed-vendor hosts, and fails clearly when neither backend is usable. The practical and published profiles remain backend-independent; hardware-specific profiles may impose an explicit backend constraint. Metadata records the resolved nvidia or amd backend. Explicit backend dry-runs remain hardware-free; default auto dry-runs perform read-only vendor detection.

test/vllm-benchmark-test.sh provides an experimental NVIDIA-only ornith-397b-mxfp4-128k profile pinned to community model olka-fi/Ornith-1.0-397B-MXFP4 revision 04940815e4ddf15e2b7cc4710e81e3cecc25540b. The canonical eight-GPU configuration retains 128K context through TP8/DCP4, FP8 KV cache with calculated scales, 0.95 GPU memory utilization, one vLLM sequence, eager and language-model-only execution, Harbor concurrency one, and no CPU offload. Hardware runs require at least 256000 MiB aggregate selected VRAM and 300 GB Docker-root free space before downloads. This community quantization is not comparable with the publisher's BF16 result and remains experimental pending a real eight-RTX-5090 smoke run.

directives.directive: Do not replace or heavily restructure test/fulltest.sh in place without real-host validation; use test/gpu-fulltest-v2.sh as the experimental lane for flow refactors first.
